text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak said the Golan Heights must be returned if we want peace in the region. He said there was no truth to rumours about the possibility of a summit between him, Syrian President Hafez al-Assad and King Fahd of Saudi Arabia, saying the time was not right for such a meeting. He also said there were no plans for a summit between Clinton, King Fahd, President Assad, King Hussein of Jordan and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He said he did not think Assad would agree to meet Netanyahu under present circumstances and after Israeli statements refusing to withdraw from the Golan.
- French President Jacques Chirac phoned President Mubarak to express his appreciation of Egypt's role.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa rejected the Israeli idea of resuming negotiations with Syria from the beginning, saying the Syrians would not accept this.

- President Hosni will this morning chair a session of the U.S.-Egyptian Presidents' Council, a private-sector advisory and lobbying group. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri and other ministers will be present.
- The Supreme Military Court will today issue its verdict in the case of the military wing of the Gama'a al-Islamiya.

- Mubarak said that he hoped the Hebron agreement would be honoured and that the U.S. role was the key and the principal element in the peace process. On Sudan, he said Sudanese Vice-President al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh came to Egypt asking for help while Islamist leader Hassan al-Turabi was insulting Egypt in the newspapers. He said there was no Ethiopian or Eritrean attack on Sudan but all Sudan's troubles are internal.
- Mubarak will meet an envoy from Russian President Boris Yeltsin today and discuss bilaeral cooperation with Russia.
- Mubarak met writers and intellectuals for two hours at the end of the opening of the Cairo International Book Fair.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said implementation of the Hebron agreement was the test of effectiveness of the peace process on the Palestinian track.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will visit Egypt within 48 hours to meet President Mubarak.
